title: Who turns from Ibrahim's way, except one who fools himself?
subtitle: Walking away from the clearest path

row.title: Allah alone
sub: never a partner, not for an instant

then: Ibn Kathir: Ibrahim {idea}worshipped Allah alone with sincerity and never committed shirk, even for an instant.{/idea} He disowned every false god, even against his own people. So who would turn from his way? {trap}Only one who wrongs and fools himself.{/trap}
now: You keep a lucky charm in the car. You check your horoscope for fun. You lean on a person as if they control your fate. {trap}Small things that dilute pure trust.{/trap} {idea}Ibrahim's way is simple: Allah alone, all the way through.{/idea}
old: A little of this and that does not hurt my faith.
new: Turning from pure worship of Allah only harms me. Ibrahim's way is the sane one.
try: Find one thing in your life you rely on as if it had power. Let it go today.

title: Submit, said his Lord. I have submitted, said Ibrahim.
subtitle: No delay between the call and the answer

row.title: I have submitted
sub: to the Lord of the worlds

then: Ibn Kathir: Allah commanded Ibrahim to be sincere and submit, and {idea}he complied perfectly.{/idea} The answer is in the past tense, as if already done. {reward}I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds.{/reward}
now: The adhan goes off while you are mid-episode. A verse tells you to forgive, and you are still angry. {idea}Ibrahim did not negotiate.{/idea} You do not have to be perfect, just quick to say yes.
old: I will submit once I feel ready.
new: Submission is answering Allah's call now, not when it feels convenient.
try: The next time you hear the adhan today, stop what you are doing within a minute.

title: Allah chose this religion for you. Do not die except as Muslims.
subtitle: The inheritance Ibrahim and Yaqub left their sons
then: Ibrahim advised his sons, and Yaqub did the same: {idea}Allah has chosen this religion for you, so do not die except as Muslims.{/idea} Ibn Kathir: do good all your life and stay on this path, so Allah grants you to die on it, since {reward}a person usually dies on the path he lived on.{/reward}
now: You plan the will, the house, the savings for the kids. What advice will you leave them? {idea}The prophets left one thing: stay with Allah to the end.{/idea} And you cannot choose your last breath, only the breaths before it.
old: I will get serious about religion closer to the end.
new: I die how I live, so I live as a Muslim now.
try: Tell your children or a younger relative one sentence about why your faith matters to you.

title: Dying, Yaqub asked his sons: What will you worship after me?
subtitle: A father's last question
then: When death came to Yaqub, {idea}he asked his children what they would worship after him.{/idea} They said: your God and the God of your fathers Ibrahim, Ismail and Ishaq, one God. Ibn Kathir cites the Prophet ﷺ: {reward}we prophets are brothers with different mothers, but one religion.{/reward}
now: Families gather in the hospital corridor and the talk turns to the house, the shop, who gets what. {idea}Yaqub's last question was different.{/idea} What do your children see you worship: Allah, or work, money and the phone?
old: The most important thing I leave behind is security for my family.
new: The most important thing I leave is my children's worship of Allah.
try: Ask your child or a young relative gently today what Allah means to them, and listen.

title: Their deeds are theirs. Yours are yours.
subtitle: Great ancestors do not cover your account
then: After Yaqub's deathbed scene, the verse closes the story. {idea}That nation has passed. They have what they earned, and you have what you earn.{/idea} Ibn Kathir cites the hadith: {trap}whoever is slowed down by his deeds will not be sped up by his lineage.{/trap}
now: Your grandfather was a hafiz. Your family goes back to a scholar. You mention it at weddings. {idea}His Quran is in his book of deeds, not yours.{/idea} Honour him by doing what he did.
old: My family's piety reflects well on me.
new: My ancestors' deeds are theirs. Only my own deeds speed me forward.
try: Pick one good habit of a righteous elder in your family and start it yourself this week.

title: Join our label to be guided? No: the upright way of Ibrahim.
subtitle: Guidance is not a club membership
then: Ibn Abbas said Abdullah bin Suriya told the Prophet ﷺ: {trap}guidance is only what we follow, so follow us.{/trap} Some Christians said the same. The answer: {idea}the religion of Ibrahim, hanif.{/idea} Abu Qilabah said hanif is what all the messengers believed, first to last.
now: Every group says: come to our circle, our sheikh, our method, and you will be guided. Some of it helps. {idea}But guidance is turning your face to Allah alone,{/idea} not wearing a badge. Ibrahim had no group but the truth.
old: If I join the right group, I am guided.
new: Guidance is the upright way of Ibrahim: Allah alone, whatever group I sit with.
try: Ask yourself honestly: do I follow my circle because it is true, or because it is mine?

title: We believe in all of Allah's prophets and make no distinction.
subtitle: A creed recited before Fajr
then: Allah tells the believers to say they believe in Him and in {idea}everything sent to every prophet, making no distinction between them.{/idea} Ibn Abbas said the Prophet ﷺ often recited this verse in the two rakahs before Fajr. When told stories from the People of the Book, he said: neither believe nor deny them; say we believe in Allah and what was sent to us.
now: Someone at work asks you about Musa or Isa and you realise you know almost nothing about them. {idea}They are your prophets too.{/idea} Believing in them all means getting to know them.
old: The other prophets belong to other religions.
new: Every prophet Allah sent is mine to believe in and learn from.
try: Tomorrow before Fajr, recite this verse in your sunnah prayer, or read a short passage about one earlier prophet.

title: If they believe as you believe, they are guided. Allah suffices.
subtitle: Their choice, your peace
then: The verse follows the creed of all prophets. {reward}If they believe in what you believe, they are guided.{/reward} If they turn away after the proof is shown, {trap}they are only in opposition.{/trap} Ibn Kathir: {idea}Allah will aid the believers and suffice them.{/idea}
now: You have explained your faith to your colleague, your neighbour, your brother in law. Some get it. Some argue, some mock. {idea}You do not have to carry their response.{/idea} Allah is enough for you.
old: If people reject my faith, I am exposed and alone.
new: Allah suffices me. Their acceptance is guidance for them; their rejection does not undo me.
try: When someone dismisses your faith today, say quietly: hasbiyallah, Allah is enough for me.

title: The colour of Allah. Whose colouring could be better?
subtitle: Let faith dye you through
then: Sibghah literally means dye or colouring. Ibn Abbas and many others said it means {idea}the religion of Allah.{/idea} Ibn Kathir links it to 30:30, Allah's fitrah, the natural way He made us on, and says: hold to it. {reward}Who could colour better than Allah?{/reward}
now: Some people wear faith like a jacket: on for Friday, off for the office. Allah's dye goes through the fabric. {idea}It shows in how you drive, how you text, how you split the bill.{/idea}
old: My faith is a part of my life, kept in its place.
new: Allah's religion is a dye meant to colour every part of me.
try: Choose one ordinary part of your day, like driving or shopping, and do it as a Muslim on purpose.

title: Argue with us about Allah? He is our Lord and yours.
subtitle: Ending a dispute with sincerity
then: The Prophet ﷺ was told to cut short the dispute: {idea}do you argue with us about Allah, when He is our Lord and your Lord?{/idea} Ibn Kathir links it to 10:41: for me my deeds, for you yours. {reward}And we are sincere to Him.{/reward} Ibrahim was told the same when his people argued with him.
now: The family debate over religion that loops every holiday. The online thread that never ends. {idea}Sometimes the strongest answer is: we each answer to the same Lord, and I am trying to be sincere to Him.{/idea} Then step back.
old: I have to keep arguing until they admit I am right.
new: We each carry our own deeds before one Lord. My task is sincerity, not winning.
try: In your next religious argument, state your view once, kindly, then end it with a sincere wish.

title: Do you know better, or does Allah?
subtitle: Hiding a testimony you hold
then: Some claimed the prophets from Ibrahim to the tribes followed their later labels. {idea}Do you know better, or does Allah?{/idea} Al-Hasan Al-Basri said their own Book stated these prophets were neither, and {trap}they testified to it, yet hid it from people.{/trap}
now: You saw what happened in the car park. You know who said what in the meeting. You were asked, and you said nothing. {trap}Hiding a testimony you hold is called a great wrong.{/trap} {idea}Allah is not unaware.{/idea}
old: Staying silent keeps me out of trouble.
new: Hiding the truth I know, when it is needed, is a serious wrong before Allah.
try: If you are holding back a truth that someone needs to be treated fairly, find a safe way to share it.

title: Said twice: they have their deeds, you have yours.
subtitle: Stop arguing about them; look at yourself

row.title: your deeds
sub: the only ones you answer for

then: The same words that closed Yaqub's story now close the argument over which label the prophets wore. Ibn Kathir: {trap}being their relatives will not suffice{/trap} unless you follow their good deeds. {idea}You will not be asked what they did. You will be asked what you did.{/idea}
now: You can spend hours debating history, which scholar was right, which group owns which prophet. {idea}None of that is on your exam.{/idea} The question is simpler and closer: did you follow them today?
old: Proving who the prophets belonged to matters a lot.
new: I will not be asked about their label, only whether I walked their way.
try: Swap one religious debate you would have today for one act the prophets did: a dua, a kindness, a prayer.
